lessons.title: Health and hygiene: malaria, safe water and vaccination
lessons.programRef: Level III — Health education: common diseases (malaria, water-borne diseases), personal and environmental hygiene, vaccination (to be checked against the official texts)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing based on the Class 6 science and health education syllabus; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Explain how malaria is transmitted and how to prevent it.
Give ways of making drinking water safe.
Explain why vaccination and good hygiene protect us.
Know what to do in case of fever.

blocks.title: Malaria
blocks.md:
**Malaria** is a disease caused by a tiny **parasite** that lives in the blood.

It is passed from person to person by the **bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito**. These mosquitoes bite mostly at **night**.

Signs of malaria: **fever**, headache, shivering, body pains, sometimes vomiting.

blocks.caption: How malaria passes from one person to another — and how a treated bed net breaks the cycle.
blocks.alt: A cycle of four boxes joined by arrows: a sick person has parasites; a female Anopheles mosquito bites him and takes parasites; the parasites grow inside the mosquito; the mosquito bites a healthy person who gets malaria. In the centre: break the cycle, sleep under a treated bed net.

blocks.title: Preventing malaria
blocks.md:
- Sleep **every night** under an **insecticide-treated bed net**.
- Remove **stagnant water** (old tins, tyres, blocked gutters): mosquitoes lay their eggs in it.
- Cover water containers and cut the bushes around the house.
- Wear long clothes in the evening.

In case of **fever**, go quickly to a **health centre**. Do not buy medicine by the roadside.

blocks.title: Safe drinking water
blocks.md:
Dirty water can carry germs that cause **cholera**, **typhoid** and **diarrhoea**.

To make water safe:
- **boil** it, let it cool, and keep it covered;
- or **filter** it, then boil or treat it (for example with water treatment tablets, as the instructions say).

Drink water from a clean, covered source or container.

blocks.title: Hygiene and vaccination
blocks.md:
- **Wash your hands with soap and water** before eating and after using the toilet.
- Keep toilets clean; put rubbish in a bin or a rubbish pit.

**Vaccination** teaches the body to defend itself against a disease before we catch it. Vaccines protect children against diseases such as **measles**, **polio**, **tuberculosis** and **tetanus**. Keep your vaccination card safe.

blocks.title: Method: answering a health question
blocks.md:
1. Name the **disease** or the danger.
2. Say **how** it spreads (mosquito, dirty water, dirty hands…).
3. Give a **way to prevent** it that blocks that path.
4. If someone is ill, say: **go to a health centre**.

blocks.title: Example 1: water in old tins
blocks.statement: Behind Amina's house there are old tins and a car tyre full of rainwater. Many mosquitoes bite the family at night. What should they do, and why?

steps.md: The danger is **malaria**. It spreads through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.
Mosquitoes lay their eggs in **stagnant water**. The tins and the tyre are breeding places.
The family should **empty** the tins and the tyre, then throw the tins away or turn them upside down. This way, fewer mosquitoes will grow.
They should also **sleep under treated bed nets**, so that mosquitoes cannot bite them at night.

blocks.answer: **Remove the stagnant water and sleep under treated bed nets: fewer mosquitoes, fewer bites, less malaria.**

blocks.title: Example 2: a fever at school
blocks.statement: Tanyi has a high fever, a headache and he is shivering. His friend says: "Just buy some tablets at the market." Is this good advice?

steps.md: Fever, headache and shivering can be signs of **malaria**, but also of other illnesses.
Medicine bought by the roadside may be **fake** or the wrong one, and the wrong dose can be dangerous.
Tanyi must go quickly to a **health centre**. A health worker can test his blood and give him the right treatment. He must take all of it, as he is told.

blocks.answer: **No. In case of fever, go to a health centre.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that **all** mosquitoes give malaria: only the **infected female Anopheles** mosquito passes it on.
- Thinking malaria comes from dirty water or from eating mangoes: it comes from a **mosquito bite**.
- Thinking clear water is always safe: clear water can still carry **germs**.
- Stopping medicine as soon as you feel better: finish the treatment.

blocks.text: Remember. Malaria is passed on by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. Sleep under a treated bed net every night and remove stagnant water. Boil drinking water and wash your hands with soap. Vaccines protect us against diseases. In case of fever, go to a health centre.

items: Male mosquitoes do not bite people: they feed on plant juices. Only females bite, because they need blood to make their eggs.
Soap does not just clean the dirt you can see: it also removes germs you cannot see.

exercises.prompt: How is malaria passed from one person to another?
choices: By the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
exercises.explanation: Malaria is transmitted by the **bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito**. It does not come from water, food or shaking hands.
exercises.method: Ask yourself: what carries the malaria parasite?
mistakes: Confusing malaria with cholera, which comes from dirty water.

exercises.prompt: True or false: boiling drinking water kills most of the germs in it.
exercises.explanation: True. Boiling kills most germs. Let the water cool and keep it in a clean, covered container.

exercises.prompt: Match each health problem with a good way to prevent it.
pairs: Sleep under a treated bed net
Drink safe water and wash hands with soap
exercises.explanation: Bed nets stop mosquito bites (malaria). Safe water and clean hands stop the germs of cholera. A vaccine protects against measles. Brushing teeth prevents tooth decay.
exercises.method: For each problem, think of how it spreads, then block that path.

exercises.prompt: True or false: water that looks clear is always safe to drink.
exercises.explanation: False. Germs are too small to be seen. Clear water can still carry germs of cholera or typhoid, so it should be boiled or treated.
mistakes: Judging water only by its colour.

exercises.prompt: Why should we empty old tins and tyres that hold rainwater near our homes?
choices: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in stagnant water
The water makes the house cold
The tins make the water salty
exercises.explanation: Mosquito eggs and larvae grow in **stagnant water**. Removing it means fewer mosquitoes and less malaria.
exercises.method: Link the place (stagnant water) with the life of the mosquito.

exercises.prompt: In a village, many children have fever. Some families drink water from a stream without boiling it, and few people sleep under bed nets.
exercises.method: Name the disease, say how it spreads, then give prevention.
mistakes: Giving a way to prevent malaria for a water-borne disease, or the other way round.

parts.prompt: Which disease, common in Cameroon, can cause fever and is linked to the lack of bed nets?
parts.explanation: Without bed nets, people are bitten by mosquitoes at night and can catch **malaria**.

parts.prompt: Which disease can the families catch by drinking the stream water without boiling it?
parts.explanation: **Cholera** is caused by germs in dirty water. Boiling the water kills these germs.

parts.prompt: What should the parents of a child with fever do?
parts.model: They should take the child to a **health centre** quickly, so that a health worker can test and treat him.
rubric: 1 mark for 'take the child to a health centre / hospital'.
parts.explanation: In case of fever, go to a health centre: do not buy roadside medicine.

parts.prompt: Give two ways the village can fight malaria.
parts.model: Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets; remove stagnant water around the houses (also accepted: cut the bushes, cover water containers).
rubric: 1/2 mark for each correct way, up to 1 mark.
parts.explanation: Bed nets stop bites; removing stagnant water stops mosquitoes from breeding.

exercises.prompt: Why are babies and young children vaccinated?
choices: To protect them against some serious diseases
exercises.explanation: A vaccine teaches the body to defend itself, so the child is **protected** against diseases such as measles or polio before meeting them.
mistakes: Thinking a vaccine is a medicine that cures an illness you already have.

exercises.prompt: Question 2 — Health and hygiene. Read the questions and answer.
exercises.method: For each disease, think of how it spreads before choosing a way to prevent it.

parts.explanation: Only the infected **female** Anopheles mosquito passes on malaria; males do not bite people.

parts.prompt: True or false: sleeping under a treated bed net helps to prevent malaria.
parts.explanation: True. The net stops mosquitoes from biting at night, and the insecticide kills them.

parts.prompt: When must you wash your hands with soap?
choices: Before eating and after using the toilet
parts.explanation: Hands carry germs we cannot see: wash them **before eating** and **after using the toilet**.

parts.prompt: Give one way of making drinking water safe.
parts.model: Boil the water (then let it cool and keep it covered). Also accepted: filter and treat it with water treatment tablets.
rubric: 1 mark for boiling, or for filtering and treating the water.
parts.explanation: Boiling kills most germs in water.

parts.prompt: Your little sister has a high fever. What should your family do?
parts.model: Take her quickly to a **health centre** (or hospital).
rubric: 1 mark for going to a health centre or hospital; 0 for buying roadside medicine.
parts.explanation: In case of fever, go to a health centre: a health worker will test her and give the right treatment.

choices: A parasite passed on by a mosquito bite
exercises.explanation: Malaria is caused by a parasite passed on by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

exercises.prompt: When do Anopheles mosquitoes bite most?
exercises.explanation: They bite mostly at night: that is why we sleep under treated bed nets.

exercises.prompt: Which disease can you catch from dirty drinking water?
exercises.explanation: Cholera is a water-borne disease: boil or treat your drinking water.

choices: It helps the body defend itself against a disease
exercises.explanation: A vaccine teaches the body to defend itself before it meets the disease.

exercises.prompt: You have a fever. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Drink a lot of cold water
exercises.explanation: In case of fever, go to a health centre to be tested and treated.
